sources.title: U.S. Energy Information Administration — Global oil market outlook

quotes.text: In addition, attacks on Saudi Arabia’s oil exports through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, [a major world oil transit chokepoint](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/report/energysecurity/article.php), reduced oil exports departing from Saudi Arabia’s Yanbu port on the Red Sea, a route which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. In August, exports out of Yanbu were down by about half from July, according to estimates from Vortexa. In response, Saudi Arabia has increased oil shipments through the Suez Canal at the north end of the Red Sea, a longer and costlier route for customers in Asia. Although Saudi Arabia has also [reportedly begun to use a series of ship-to-ship transfers](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/aramco-offers-more-oil-outside-hormuz-with-some-cargoes-heading-china-2026-08-26/) outside of the Persian Gulf, we expect that the constrained Red Sea shipping channel will limit Saudi Arabia’s supply in the near term until global shipping flows adjust.

sources.title: The Guardian — Satellite images show extent of damage to major Saudi pipeline

quotes.text: Satellite photos released on Sunday night appeared to show a pumping station on the key 1,200km (745-mile) Saudi east-west pipeline charred and badly damaged, after drone attacks on Friday.

Since the drone attacks forced the shutdown of the pipeline, Riyadh has yet to provide full details about the extent of the damage or how long the ​route will stay offline. The Saudis [blamed the attack on drones launched by militants in Iraq](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/12/saudi-arabia-shuts-down-oil-pipeline-blaming-drones-from-iraq).
